claim: The nucleosome is composed of ~150 bp of DNA wrapped around an octamer of histone proteins.
source: The smallest unit of chromatin is the nucleosome, a DNA-protein complex composed of ~150 bp of DNA wrapped around an octamer of histone proteins (Luger et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Luger et al., 1997, which is a foundational structural study of the nucleosome.

claim: ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling enzymes play essential roles in transcription, DNA replication, and DNA repair.
source: Underscoring their central role in chromatin regulation, remodeling enzymes play essential roles in many processes including transcription, DNA replication, and DNA repair (Falbo and Shen, 2006; Hota and Bruneau, 2016; Price and D'Andrea, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Chromatin remodelers are members of the SF2 superfamily of nucleic acid motors.
source: Chromatin remodelers are members of the SF2 superfamily of nucleic acid motors, which catalyze noncovalent changes to nucleic acid substrates (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2016.

claim: Maximal remodeling by ISWI family remodelers requires DNA flanking the nucleosome and the N-terminal tail of histone H4.
source: For example, maximal remodeling by ISWI family remodelers, which primarily slide nucleosomes, requires DNA flanking the nucleosome and the N-terminal tail of histone H4 (Clapier et al., 2001; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Clapier et al., 2001 and Yang et al., 2006.

claim: Maximal remodeling by SWI/SNF family remodelers does not require flanking DNA or the H4 tail.
source: Conversely, maximal remodeling by SWI/SNF family remodelers, which carry out the most diverse set of changes to nucleosome structure, does not require these nucleosomal epitopes (Guyon et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Guyon et al., 1999.

claim: Chromatin remodelers are held in an inactive conformation by family-specific autoinhibitory motifs in the ground state.
source: Some important insights have come from biochemical analyses and structures of remodelers in the absence of nucleosomes, which suggest that in the ground state, chromatin remodelers are held in an inactive conformation by family-specific autoinhibitory motifs (Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Hauk et al., 2010; Xia et al., 2016; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Many proteins interact with a conserved acidic patch formed by histones H2A and H2B on the top surface of the nucleosome.
source: At the same time, structures of several nucleosome-protein complexes are revealing that many of these proteins interact with a conserved acidic patch formed by histones H2A and H2B on the top surface of the nucleosome (McGinty and Tan, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McGinty and Tan, 2016.

claim: Proteins interact with the acidic patch using an 'arginine anchor' which nestles into a pocket formed by the α1–2 helices of histone H2A.
source: These proteins interact with the acidic patch using an 'arginine anchor' which nestles into a pocket formed by the α1–2 helices of histone H2A (McGinty and Tan, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McGinty and Tan, 2016.

claim: Mutating the acidic patch reduces the activity of ISWI, SWI/SNF and some CHD family remodeling enzymes.
source: Indeed recent work has indicated that mutating the acidic patch reduces the activity of ISWI, SWI/SNF and some CHD family remodeling enzymes (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: APM nucleosomes are centered substantially slower than WT nucleosomes under conditions where SNF2h is in excess of nucleosomes.
source: APM nucleosomes are centered substantially slower than WT nucleosomes under conditions where SNF2h is in excess of nucleosomes (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Kmapp is affected substantially less by mutation of the acidic patch than the maximal rate constant for remodeling, kmax (61 nM to 280 nM, corresponding to ~4.5 fold increased Kmapp, versus 2.5 min−1 to 0.012 min−1, corresponding to ~200 fold reduced kmax).
source: Interestingly however, Kmapp is affected substantially less by mutation of the acidic patch than the maximal rate constant for remodeling, kmax (Figure 1D, 61 nM to 280 nM, corresponding to ~4.5 fold increased Kmapp, versus 2.5 min−1 to 0.012 min−1, corresponding to ~200 fold reduced kmax).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: At saturating nucleosome concentrations, APM nucleosomes stimulate ATP hydrolysis 4-fold less than WT.
source: At saturating nucleosome concentrations, APM nucleosomes stimulate ATP hydrolysis 4-fold less than WT (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The acidic patch plays a critical role in coupling ATP hydrolysis to remodeling after the binding step.
source: Together, these results imply that the acidic patch plays a critical role in coupling ATP hydrolysis to remodeling after the binding step.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that the acidic patch affects kmax more than Kmapp and reduces ATP hydrolysis stimulation.

claim: The presence of the LANA peptide dramatically slows remodeling by SNF2h in a dose-dependent manner (~200 fold reduction in rate constant at 50 µM LANA peptide).
source: The presence of the LANA peptide dramatically slows remodeling by SNF2h in a dose-dependent manner (~200 fold reduction in rate constant at 50 µM LANA peptide), while a peptide with a mutant arginine anchor does not have a detectable inhibitory effect (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: A KI of 1.2 µM was measured for inhibition by the LANA peptide, within 5-fold of its published affinity for the nucleosome.
source: We measured a KI of 1.2 µM for inhibition by the LANA peptide, within 5-fold of its published affinity for the nucleosome (Figure 1F) (Fang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and a citation to Fang et al., 2016.

claim: Remodeling by SNF2h requires an interaction with the acidic patch that is mutually exclusive with the binding of acidic patch interacting factors such as the LANA peptide.
source: These results indicate that remodeling by SNF2h requires an interaction with the acidic patch that is mutually exclusive with the binding of acidic patch interacting factors such as the LANA peptide.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that the LANA peptide inhibits remodeling by SNF2h.

claim: Except for residue E64, all the single alanine mutants have comparable defects as the four point mutants combined.
source: Interestingly, except for residue E64, all the single alanine mutants have comparable defects as the four point mutants combined (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Three of the four acidic patch residues tested act cooperatively to promote sliding by SNF2h.
source: This observation suggests that three of the four acidic patch residues tested here act cooperatively to promote sliding by SNF2h.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that single mutants have comparable defects to the four-point mutant.

claim: Cross-links between the H4 tail and RecA lobe 2 of SNF2h are strongly enhanced in the ADP•BeFx state.
source: Cross-links between the H4 tail and RecA lobe 2 of SNF2h are strongly enhanced in the ADP•BeFx state (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The ADP•BeFx state promotes specific cross-links between the H2A/H2B acidic patch and lysines in the extended AutoN region, RecA lobe 1, the NegC region, and the DNA binding HAND-SANT-SLIDE (HSS) region of SNF2h.
source: We also found that the ADP•BeFx state promotes specific cross-links between the H2A/H2B acidic patch and lysines in the extended AutoN region, RecA lobe 1, the NegC region, and the DNA binding HAND-SANT-SLIDE (HSS) region of SNF2h (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: 2RA SNF2h remodels WT nucleosomes ~ 2 fold faster than WT SNF2h.
source: Consistent with previous reports, 2RA SNF2h remodels WT nucleosomes ~ 2 fold faster than WT SNF2h (Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Clapier and Cairns, 2012 and Yan et al., 2016.

claim: 2RA SNF2h remodels APM nucleosomes ~ 50 fold faster than WT SNF2h.
source: However, 2RA SNF2h remodels APM nucleosomes ~ 50 fold faster than WT SNF2h (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The acidic patch contributes to relief of autoinhibition by R142 and R144 in AutoN.
source: Together, these data suggest that the acidic patch contributes to relief of autoinhibition by R142 and R144 in AutoN.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that the 2RA mutation rescues the defect caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: mNegC SNF2h slides WT 0/60 nucleosomes ~ 1.2 fold faster than WT SNF2h.
source: Consistent with previous work, mNegC SNF2h slides WT 0/60 nucleosomes ~ 1.2 fold faster than WT SNF2h (Figure 2E and F) (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F and a citation to Leonard and Narlikar, 2015.

claim: mNegC SNF2h slides APM nucleosomes ~ 100 fold faster than WT SNF2h.
source: However, mNegC SNF2h slides APM nucleosomes ~ 100 fold faster than WT SNF2h (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Sliding of APM nucleosomes by mNegC SNF2h is only ~2 fold slower than WT nucleosomes.
source: As a result, sliding of APM nucleosomes by mNegC SNF2h is only ~2 fold slower than WT nucleosomes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that mNegC mutation rescues the defect caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: The mNegC mutation almost completely rescues the defect of the acidic patch mutation.
source: Thus the mNegC mutation almost completely rescues the defect of the acidic patch mutation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that mNegC SNF2h remodels APM nucleosomes almost as fast as WT nucleosomes.

claim: Residues in NegC link activation of nucleosome sliding to acidic patch recognition.
source: These results suggest that residues in NegC also link activation of nucleosome sliding to acidic patch recognition.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that mNegC mutation rescues the defect caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: Addition of the LANA peptide substantially reduced crosslinks between the H2A acidic patch and both AutoN and NegC.
source: Addition of the LANA peptide substantially reduced crosslinks between the H2A acidic patch and both AutoN and NegC (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Crosslinks between the HSS and the acidic patch were less strongly affected by LANA addition.
source: In contrast, crosslinks between the HSS and the acidic patch were less strongly affected by LANA addition (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Acidic patch recognition is strongly linked to relief of autoinhibition by NegC and AutoN for nucleosome sliding by SNF2h.
source: Together, these data suggest that acidic patch recognition is strongly linked to relief of autoinhibition by NegC and AutoN for nucleosome sliding by SNF2h.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that mutations in AutoN and NegC rescue defects caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: Activation of SNF2h involves conformational changes that bring both AutoN and NegC autoinhibitory domains and the HSS in closer proximity to the acidic patch.
source: Furthermore, activation of SNF2h involves conformational changes that bring both of these autoinhibitory domains and the HSS in closer proximity to the acidic patch.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the crosslinking mass spectrometry data showing increased crosslinks between these domains and the acidic patch in the ADP•BeFx state.

claim: SNF2h slides nucleosomes in a series of alternating phases: a 'pause' phase, in which FRET (and therefore nucleosome position) remain constant, and a 'translocation' phase, in which the nucleosome is moved relative to the DNA end.
source: A key insight revealed by these smFRET studies is that ISWI family remodelers do not slide nucleosomes in a continuous manner, such that FRET decreases continuously over time, but rather in a series of alternating phases: a 'pause' phase, in which FRET (and therefore nucleosome position) remain constant, and a 'translocation' phase, in which the nucleosome is moved relative to the DNA end.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous smFRET studies of ISWI family remodelers.

claim: The overall remodeling rates observed in ensemble assays are dominated by the durations of the pause phases, not the translocation rate itself.
source: These repeating pause phases, which so far appear to be specific to ISWI, are essential to our understanding of the mechanism of action of ISWI remodelers, because the overall remodeling rates observed in ensemble assays are dominated by the durations of the pause phases, not the translocation rate itself.
evidence: This claim is based on previous smFRET studies of ISWI family remodelers.

claim: Substrate cues such as the H4 tail and flanking DNA have been shown to be sensed in the pause phase, not the translocation phase, for ISWI family remodelers.
source: Moreover, substrate cues such as the H4 tail and flanking DNA have been shown to be sensed in the pause phase, not the translocation phase, for ISWI family remodelers (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hwang et al., 2014.

claim: SNF2h alone shares the alternating pause and translocation behavior at the single-molecule level.
source: As shown in Figure 3B, we find that SNF2h alone, like the ACF complex and the yeast ISWI enzymes, shares this alternating pause and translocation behavior at the single-molecule level.
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Remodeling of E64R nucleosomes by SNF2h proceeds through the same alternating pause and translocation phases as does remodeling of WT nucleosomes.
source: As shown in the example trajectories in Figure 3C, remodeling of E64R nucleosomes by SNF2h proceeds through the same alternating pause and translocation phases as does remodeling of WT nucleosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The pauses are noticeably longer with E64R nucleosomes, by at least a factor of 2.
source: However, the pauses are noticeably longer with E64R nucleosomes, by at least a factor of 2 (Figure 3D), indicating that the acidic patch epitope, like other substrate cues, is indeed sensed during the regulatory pause phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The acidic patch epitope is sensed during the regulatory pause phase.
source: However, the pauses are noticeably longer with E64R nucleosomes, by at least a factor of 2 (Figure 3D), indicating that the acidic patch epitope, like other substrate cues, is indeed sensed during the regulatory pause phase.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the smFRET data showing longer pause durations with E64R nucleosomes.

claim: 2RA SNF2h remodels WT nucleosomes slightly faster than SNF2h by reducing pause durations.
source: In agreement with our ensemble results (Figure 2C), 2RA SNF2h remodels WT nucleosomes slightly faster than SNF2h by reducing pause durations (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 2RA rescues the deleterious effect of the E64R acidic patch mutation, by nearly restoring wild-type pause durations.
source: Furthermore, 2RA rescues the deleterious effect of the E64R acidic patch mutation, by nearly restoring wild-type pause durations (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: SNF2h moves E64R nucleosomes a shorter distance in each translocation phase compared to WT nucleosomes.
source: However, SNF2h moves E64R nucleosomes a shorter distance in each translocation phase, as indicated by the leftward shift of the cumulative distributions in the red curves of Figure 3E, relative to the black curves (on average, E64R nucleosomes move about 6 bp in the first translocation and about 4 bp in the second (Figure 3—figure supplement 3)).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mutation of AutoN has little effect on the step size in the context of WT nucleosomes, but largely restores the step size in the context of E64R nucleosomes to that of SNF2h with WT nucleosomes.
source: Mutation of AutoN has little effect on the step size in the context of WT nucleosomes, but largely restores the step size in the context of E64R nucleosomes to that of SNF2h with WT nucleosomes (Figure 3E, magenta and blue curves).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: With E64R nucleosomes, SNF2h takes fewer elementary steps in succession during the translocation phase, before entering a new pause phase.
source: Given that ISWI family remodelers have been shown to translocate a nucleosome in elementary steps of 1–2 bp (Deindl et al., 2013), our results suggest that with E64R nucleosomes, SNF2h takes fewer of these elementary steps in succession during the translocation phase, before entering a new pause phase.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the smFRET data showing smaller step sizes with E64R nucleosomes and a citation to Deindl et al., 2013.

claim: The major contributions to the remodeling defects observed with SNF2h and APM nucleosomes can be attributed to two effects: first, an increase in pause duration, and second, a decrease in the distance travelled per translocation event.
source: The major contributions to the remodeling defects observed with SNF2h and APM nucleosomes can therefore be attributed to two effects: first, an increase in pause duration, and second, a decrease in the distance travelled per translocation event, meaning that there are more (and longer) pauses in APM remodeling reactions per unit distance that the nucleosome is moved.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the smFRET data showing increased pause durations and decreased step sizes with E64R nucleosomes.

claim: Both the increase in pause duration and the decrease in step size are rescued by the 2RA mutation of the AutoN motif of SNF2h.
source: Both of these effects are rescued by the 2RA mutation of the AutoN motif of SNF2h.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the smFRET data showing that 2RA mutation rescues both pause duration and step size defects.

claim: The acidic patch is important for relieving autoinhibition by AutoN and thereby promoting exit from the pause phase.
source: We propose that the acidic patch is important for relieving autoinhibition by AutoN and thereby promoting exit from the pause phase.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental results showing that acidic patch mutations increase pause durations and that 2RA mutation rescues this defect.

claim: The acidic patch is involved in keeping AutoN out of the active site until the nucleosome has been translocated to the full extent (~8 bp initially,~5 bp subsequently) and a new pause phase is entered.
source: Further, we propose that the acidic patch is also involved in keeping AutoN out of the active site until the nucleosome has been translocated to the full extent (~8 bp initially,~5 bp subsequently) and a new pause phase is entered (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental results showing that acidic patch mutations decrease step sizes and that 2RA mutation rescues this defect.

claim: At saturating concentrations of ACF, ACF slides APM nucleosomes 10-fold more slowly than WT.
source: At saturating concentrations of ACF, where binding does not contribute to the overall remodeling rate, ACF slides APM nucleosomes 10-fold more slowly than WT (Figure 4A), indicating that ACF also uses the acidic patch in a step after binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ACF also uses the acidic patch in a step after binding.
source: At saturating concentrations of ACF, where binding does not contribute to the overall remodeling rate, ACF slides APM nucleosomes 10-fold more slowly than WT (Figure 4A), indicating that ACF also uses the acidic patch in a step after binding.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that ACF remodels APM nucleosomes more slowly at saturating concentrations.

claim: ACF is less dependent on the acidic patch compared to SNF2h alone.
source: However, consistent with previous work, ACF is less dependent on the acidic patch compared to SNF2h alone (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: INO80 slides APM nucleosomes ~ 200 fold more slowly than WT nucleosomes at saturating concentrations.
source: Interestingly, we find that INO80 slides APM nucleosomes ~ 200 fold more slowly than WT nucleosomes at saturating concentrations (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: INO80 also uses the acidic patch post-binding, but is more dependent on the acidic patch than the ACF complex.
source: This result indicates that INO80 also uses the acidic patch post-binding, but is more dependent on the acidic patch than the ACF complex.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that INO80 remodels APM nucleosomes much more slowly at saturating concentrations.

claim: The acidic patch is used post-binding in order to activate remodeling by both INO80 and ISWI family remodelers.
source: In this study, we investigate the role of the highly conserved H2A acidic patch in chromatin remodeling by ISWI enzymes. We find that the acidic patch is used post-binding in order to activate remodeling by both INO80 and ISWI family remodelers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that acidic patch mutations affect kmax more than Kmapp for both SNF2h and INO80.

claim: The acidic patch is used by SNF2h to relieve autoinhibition by the conserved AutoN and NegC motifs.
source: Furthermore, using a combination of ensemble and single molecule methods, we show that the acidic patch is used by SNF2h to relieve autoinhibition by the conserved AutoN and NegC motifs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that mutations in AutoN and NegC rescue defects caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: The ATPase domain of ISWI enzymes is thought to bind and translocate DNA two helical turns from the nucleosomal dyad (SHL ± 2).
source: On the basis of crosslinking and footprinting studies, the ATPase domain of ISWI enzymes is thought to bind and translocate DNA two helical turns from the nucleosomal dyad (SHL ± 2) (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Kagalwala et al., 2004; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: The C-terminal HAND-SANT-SLIDE (HSS) domain mediates flanking DNA recognition.
source: The C-terminal HAND-SANT-SLIDE (HSS) domain mediates flanking DNA recognition, while the H4 tail appears to be directly recognized by the second RecA lobe within the ATPase domain (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dang and Bartholomew, 2007 and Yan et al., 2016.

claim: The H4 tail appears to be directly recognized by the second RecA lobe within the ATPase domain.
source: The C-terminal HAND-SANT-SLIDE (HSS) domain mediates flanking DNA recognition, while the H4 tail appears to be directly recognized by the second RecA lobe within the ATPase domain (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dang and Bartholomew, 2007 and Yan et al., 2016.

claim: The acidic patch resides on a surface near SHL ± 6, far from where the ATPase domain engages the nucleosome.
source: The acidic patch resides on a surface near SHL ± 6, far from where the ATPase domain engages the nucleosome.
evidence: This claim is based on structural knowledge of the nucleosome and the location of the acidic patch.

claim: Two known autoinhibitory regions of ISWI enzymes, the AutoN region and the NegC region, functionally interact with the acidic patch.
source: Our results suggest that two known autoinhibitory regions of ISWI enzymes, the AutoN region and the NegC region, functionally interact with the acidic patch, because mutating these regions dramatically reduces the dependence of SNF2h on the acidic patch for sliding.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that mutations in AutoN and NegC rescue defects caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: A large role of the acidic patch is to relieve autoinhibition by both AutoN and NegC.
source: This suggests that a large role of the acidic patch is to relieve autoinhibition by both AutoN and NegC.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that mutations in AutoN and NegC rescue defects caused by acidic patch mutations.

claim: Activation of the enzyme places residues within both AutoN and NegC near the acidic patch.
source: While we do not have evidence for a direct interaction between the acidic patch and the two arginines in AutoN, our cross-linking mass spectrometry data suggests that activation of the enzyme places residues within both AutoN and NegC near this location.
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data showing increased crosslinks between AutoN/NegC and the acidic patch in the ADP•BeFx state.

claim: The AutoN region inhibits the transition from the pause phase to the translocation phase.
source: Our smFRET work here and previous smFRET work suggests that the AutoN region inhibits the transition from the pause phase to the translocation phase (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data and a citation to Hwang et al., 2014.

claim: Flanking DNA and the H4 tail are both sensed in the pause phase.
source: It has been shown that flanking DNA and the H4 tail are both sensed in the pause phase (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hwang et al., 2014.

claim: The NegC region inhibits the transition between a flanking DNA sensing state of SNF2h and a translocation competent state of SNF2h.
source: Further, previous ensemble work has suggested that the NegC region inhibits the transition between a flanking DNA sensing state of SNF2h and a translocation competent state of SNF2h (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Leonard and Narlikar, 2015.

claim: The acidic patch helps promote the translocation competent state of SNF2h by providing an alternative binding site for NegC and AutoN.
source: We therefore propose that the acidic patch helps promote the translocation competent state of SNF2h by providing an alternative binding site for NegC and AutoN (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental results showing that acidic patch mutations affect remodeling and that mutations in AutoN and NegC rescue these defects.

claim: Translocation is interrupted by premature reversion of the enzyme to the autoinhibited state in the absence of stabilizing interactions with the acidic patch.
source: We hypothesize that translocation is interrupted by premature reversion of the enzyme to the autoinhibited state in the absence of stabilizing interactions with the acidic patch (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental results showing that acidic patch mutations decrease step sizes.

claim: The acidic patch provides a binding surface for NegC and AutoN that sequesters these regions from inhibiting SNF2h.
source: Our results lead to a model in which the acidic patch provides a binding surface for NegC and AutoN that sequesters these regions from inhibiting SNF2h (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental results showing that acidic patch mutations affect remodeling and that mutations in AutoN and NegC rescue these defects.

claim: The acidic patch increases Kmapp for SNF2h by ~5 fold.
source: The acidic patch increases Kmapp for SNF2h by ~5 fold, suggesting that interactions with the acidic patch also stabilize SNF2h binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that APM nucleosomes have a ~4.5 fold increased Kmapp.

claim: Interactions with the acidic patch stabilize SNF2h binding.
source: The acidic patch increases Kmapp for SNF2h by ~5 fold, suggesting that interactions with the acidic patch also stabilize SNF2h binding.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that APM nucleosomes have an increased Kmapp.

claim: The acidic patch appears to be used in at least two distinct steps of the SNF2h remodeling reaction.
source: Thus the acidic patch appears to be used in at least two distinct steps of the SNF2h remodeling reaction.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that the acidic patch affects both Kmapp and kmax.

claim: AutoN mutations additively increase Kmapp beyond solely mutating the acidic patch.
source: In contrast to the rescuing effects of AutoN mutations on maximal activity, AutoN mutations additively increase Kmapp beyond solely mutating the acidic patch (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: AutoN and the acidic patch do not cooperate in the ground state.
source: This suggests that AutoN and the acidic patch do not cooperate in the ground state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that AutoN mutations additively increase Kmapp beyond solely mutating the acidic patch.

claim: Different SNF2h domains contact the acidic patch in different steps of the remodeling reaction.
source: It is thus possible that different SNF2h domains contact the acidic patch in different steps of the remodeling reaction.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that the acidic patch affects both binding and catalysis, and that AutoN and the acidic patch do not cooperate in the ground state.

claim: SNF2h undergoes a large conformational change prior to adopting a translocation competent state that repositions the C-terminus from binding flanking DNA towards binding the nucleosome core.
source: Based on previous work, we have hypothesized that SNF2h undergoes a large conformational change prior to adopting a translocation competent state that repositions the C-terminus from binding flanking DNA towards binding the nucleosome core (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on previous work cited as Leonard and Narlikar, 2015.

claim: Crosslinks between the H2A/H2B acidic patch and the SANT domain increase in the ADP•BeFx-bound state compared to the ADP-bound state.
source: We find that crosslinks between the H2A/H2B acidic patch and the SANT domain increase in the ADP•BeFx-bound state compared to the ADP-bound state (Figure 2B), consistent with the HSS binding to the nucleosome core.
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The location of the HSS in the ADP•BeFx-bound state is not strongly dependent on direct contacts with the residues contacted by the LANA peptide.
source: Interestingly, these crosslinks are not substantially reduced by LANA peptide binding, suggesting that the location of the HSS in the ADP•BeFx-bound state is not strongly dependent on direct contacts with the residues contacted by the LANA peptide (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the crosslinking mass spectrometry data showing that LANA peptide does not substantially reduce HSS-acidic patch crosslinks.

claim: The SANT domain and LANA peptide may occupy adjacent regions on the nucleosome core.
source: This result raises the possibility that the SANT domain and LANA peptide occupy adjacent regions on the nucleosome core.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that LANA peptide does not substantially reduce HSS-acidic patch crosslinks.

claim: LANA binding directly or indirectly displaces NegC and AutoN from the nucleosome.
source: In contrast, NegC and AutoN crosslinks to the acidic patch are substantially reduced by the LANA peptide, suggesting LANA binding directly or indirectly displaces these regions from the nucleosome.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the crosslinking mass spectrometry data showing that LANA peptide substantially reduces NegC and AutoN crosslinks to the acidic patch.

claim: The key accessory regions of SNF2h namely, HSS, NegC and AutoN, are all positioned near the acidic patch in the activated state.
source: Overall our results suggest that the key accessory regions of SNF2h namely, HSS, NegC and AutoN, are all positioned near the acidic patch in the activated state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the crosslinking mass spectrometry data showing increased crosslinks between these regions and the acidic patch in the ADP•BeFx state.

claim: Crosslinks between the C-terminus of SNF2h and NegC increase in the ADP•BeFx state.
source: In agreement with this observation, crosslinks between the C-terminus of SNF2h and NegC increase in the ADP•BeFx state (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Contacts between accessory domains may play a role in promoting the translocation-competent state.
source: The close positioning of multiple SNF2h accessory domains near the acidic patch raises the possibility that contacts between accessory domains may play a role in promoting the translocation-competent state.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that multiple accessory domains are positioned near the acidic patch in the activated state.

claim: The human ISWI complex, ACF, requires the acidic patch for maximal activity but shows a ~ 20 fold smaller defect upon mutation of the acidic patch than observed with SNF2h alone.
source: Here we find that the human ISWI complex, ACF, requires the acidic patch for maximal activity but shows a ~ 20 fold smaller defect upon mutation of the acidic patch than observed with SNF2h alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing the effects of acidic patch mutations on ACF and SNF2h.

claim: The accessory protein Acf1 alters the mechanism of relief of autoinhibition by the acidic patch in a manner that makes the reaction less dependent on the acidic patch.
source: In particular, our results suggest that the accessory protein Acf1 alters the mechanism of relief of autoinhibition by the acidic patch in a manner that makes the reaction less dependent on the acidic patch, perhaps by providing an alternative binding partner for the AutoN and NegC domains.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that ACF is less dependent on the acidic patch than SNF2h alone.

claim: INO80 family remodelers are insensitive to the presence of the H4 tail.
source: Importantly, INO80 family remodelers are insensitive to the presence of the H4 tail and no AutoN-like or NegC like motif has been identified in the ATPase subunit of INO80 (Udugama et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Udugama et al., 2011.

claim: No AutoN-like or NegC like motif has been identified in the ATPase subunit of INO80.
source: Importantly, INO80 family remodelers are insensitive to the presence of the H4 tail and no AutoN-like or NegC like motif has been identified in the ATPase subunit of INO80 (Udugama et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Udugama et al., 2011.

claim: The acidic patch must activate INO80 through a mechanism distinct from ISWI complexes.
source: The acidic patch must then activate INO80 through a mechanism distinct from ISWI complexes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that INO80 lacks AutoN and NegC motifs but is still dependent on the acidic patch.

claim: Several families of chromatin remodelers require the acidic patch for remodeling.
source: Combined with previous results (Dann et al., 2017), our results suggest that several families of chromatin remodelers require the acidic patch for remodeling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: Yeast CHD1 can remodel nucleosomes largely independent of the acidic patch.
source: However, it is possible that this surface is not a universal requirement for chromatin remodeling, as yeast CHD1 can remodel nucleosomes largely independent of the acidic patch (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Levendosky et al., 2016.

claim: CHD1 uses an unidentified aspect of the histone H2A/H2B dimer to promote remodeling.
source: CHD1 instead uses an unidentified aspect of the histone H2A/H2B dimer to promote remodeling (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Levendosky et al., 2016.

claim: The enormous difference in dependence on the acidic patch between yeast CHD1 and ISWI enzymes raises the possibility that these families remodel nucleosomes through distinct mechanisms.
source: However, the enormous difference in dependence on the acidic patch between yeast CHD1 and ISWI enzymes raise the possibility that these families remodel nucleosomes through distinct mechanisms (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that CHD1 and ISWI have different dependencies on the acidic patch.

claim: CHD family remodelers do not appear to possess an AutoN motif.
source: Importantly, while yeast CHD1 shares domains with ISWI remodelers such as the SANT-SLIDE domains at the C-terminus and a version of the NegC region, called the C-terminal bridge (Hauk et al., 2010; Ryan et al., 2011), CHD family remodelers do not appear to possess an AutoN motif.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hauk et al., 2010 and Ryan et al., 2011.

claim: Remodelers like CHD1 have an N-terminal double chromodomain which has an analogous role as an autoinhibitiory domain that is relieved by H4 tail binding.
source: Instead, remodelers like CHD1 have an N-terminal double chromodomain which has an analogous role as an autoinhibitiory domain that is relieved by H4 tail binding (Hauk et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hauk et al., 2010.

claim: Nucleosomes lacking histone H2A-H2B dimers or containing a modified acidic patch through histone variants or covalent modifications may be recognized and remodeled differently than canonical nucleosomes by different remodelers.
source: At a primary level, the requirement of the acidic patch provides a powerful means for remodelers to sense and respond to chromatin structure and nucleosome content. Thus, nucleosomes lacking histone H2A-H2B dimers or containing a modified acidic patch through histone variants or covalent modifications may be recognized and remodeled differently than canonical nucleosomes by different remodelers (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that the acidic patch is important for remodeling and a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: Nucleosomes containing histone H2Az, which have an extended acidic patch, are remodeled ~2 fold faster by ISWI complexes than canonical nucleosomes.
source: Consistent with this possibility, nucleosomes containing histone H2Az, which have an extended acidic patch, are remodeled ~2 fold faster by ISWI complexes than canonical nucleosomes (Goldman et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Goldman et al., 2010.

claim: INO80 preferentially slides H2AZ nucleosomes over H2A nucleosomes.
source: Analogously, recent work has shown that INO80 preferentially slides H2AZ nucleosomes over H2A nucleosomes (Brahma et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brahma et al., 2017.

claim: Remodelers and other chromatin binding proteins compete for access to the acidic patch.
source: Finally, given the growing list of factors that recognize the acidic patch, it is likely that remodelers and other chromatin binding proteins compete for access to the acidic patch.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that many factors recognize the acidic patch.

claim: Binding by the LANA peptide to the acidic patch competes for remodeling by SNF2h.
source: Indeed, binding by the LANA peptide to the acidic patch competes for remodeling by SNF2h.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that the LANA peptide inhibits remodeling by SNF2h.

claim: Sensitivity to the acidic patch could be a general mechanism to regulate the outcome of chromatin remodeling at loci where remodelers and other factors are jostling for access to their chromatin substrates.
source: Sensitivity to the acidic patch could be a general mechanism to regulate the outcome of chromatin remodeling at loci where remodelers and other factors are jostling for access to their chromatin substrates.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that the acidic patch is important for remodeling and that multiple factors compete for access to it.

claim: SNF2h moves WT nucleosomes with an initial large step (~8 bp) followed by a smaller (~5 bp) step.
source: Like other ISWI family remodelers, SNF2h moves WT nucleosomes with an initial large step (~8 bp) followed by a smaller (~5 bp) step (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3; [Blosser et al., 2009; Deindl et al., 2013]).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and citations to Blosser et al., 2009 and Deindl et al., 2013.

claim: The human ISWI ATPase, SNF2h, preferentially slides nucleosomes toward longer flanking DNA.
source: The human ISWI ATPase, SNF2h, preferentially slides nucleosomes toward longer flanking DNA (Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2006.

claim: SNF2h slides mononucleosomes towards the center of a DNA strand.
source: As a consequence of this activity, SNF2h slides mononucleosomes towards the center of a DNA strand, an activity that can be detected by a native gel mobility assay (Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2006.

claim: Mutating residues in the nucleosome acidic patch reduces the ability of SNF2h to expose nucleosomal DNA to restriction enzymes.
source: Recent work has shown that mutating residues in the nucleosome acidic patch reduces the ability of SNF2h to expose nucleosomal DNA to restriction enzymes (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: The LANA peptide has previously been shown to interact directly with the acidic patch via an arginine anchor.
source: We used a peptide derived from the latency associated nuclear antigen (LANA) from Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus that has previously been shown to interact directly with the acidic patch via an arginine anchor (Barbera et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Barbera et al., 2006.

claim: The LANA peptide can inhibit the restriction enzyme accessibility activity of the SNF2h containing complex, ACF.
source: The results are also consistent with recent work showing that the LANA peptide can inhibit the restriction enzyme accessibility activity of the SNF2h containing complex, ACF (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: ADP•BeFx mimics an activated state of the SNF2h-nucleosome complex.
source: In previous work we have shown that ADP•BeFx mimics an activated state of the SNF2h-nucleosome complex (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015; Racki et al., 2014; Sinha et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Leonard and Narlikar, 2015; Racki et al., 2014; and Sinha et al., 2017.

claim: The H4 tail activates ISWI remodelers and promotes a restricted active site conformation in the presence of ADP•BeFx.
source: This result is consistent with previous work showing that the H4 tail activates ISWI remodelers and promotes a restricted active site conformation in the presence of ADP•BeFx (Clapier et al., 2001; Hamiche et al., 2001; Racki et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Clapier et al., 2001; Hamiche et al., 2001; and Racki et al., 2014.

claim: NegC is an autoinhibitory region of SNF2h that imposes flanking DNA length sensitivity on SNF2h by specifically slowing down remodeling of nucleosomes without flanking DNA.
source: NegC is another autoinhibitory region of SNF2h that imposes flanking DNA length sensitivity on SNF2h by specifically slowing down remodeling of nucleosomes without flanking DNA (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Leonard and Narlikar, 2015.

claim: Autoinhibition by the two arginine residues in AutoN is relieved by a basic patch on the H4 tail.
source: Autoinhibition by these arginine residues is relieved by a basic patch on the H4 tail, a nucleosomal epitope essential for maximal remodeling by ISWI-family remodelers (Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Clapier et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Clapier and Cairns, 2012 and Clapier et al., 2002.

claim: SNF2h remodels nucleosomes as a dimer at saturating enzyme concentrations.
source: Although SNF2h remodels nucleosomes as a dimer at saturating enzyme concentrations (Blosser et al., 2009; Racki et al., 2009), in this model we display only one of the protomers for simplicity.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blosser et al., 2009 and Racki et al., 2009.

claim: ACF is a heterodimer of the ISWI ATPase subunit (SNF2h in humans) and the accessory subunit Acf1.
source: ACF is a heterodimer of the ISWI ATPase subunit (SNF2h in humans) and the accessory subunit Acf1, and is implicated in gene repression, DNA replication, and DNA repair (Collins et al., 2002; Fyodorov et al., 2004; Lan et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Collins et al., 2002; Fyodorov et al., 2004; and Lan et al., 2010.

claim: Human ACF has the same core activity as SNF2h, but displays greater nucleosome affinity, enhanced sliding rates, and better kinetic discrimination of flanking DNA length.
source: Biochemically, human ACF has the same core activity as SNF2h, but displays greater nucleosome affinity, enhanced sliding rates, and better kinetic discrimination of flanking DNA length (He et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to He et al., 2006 and Yang et al., 2006.

claim: In the context of ACF, AutoN regulates flanking DNA length sensing through interaction of an Acf1-specific domain called WAC.
source: For instance, in the context of ACF, AutoN regulates flanking DNA length sensing through interaction of an Acf1-specific domain called WAC (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hwang et al., 2014.

claim: Mutating the nucleosomal acidic patch causes a smaller defect in remodeling by ACF compared to SNF2h.
source: Furthermore, recent work has suggested that mutating the nucleosomal acidic patch causes a smaller defect in remodeling by ACF compared to SNF2h (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: While some CHD family remodelers slide nucleosomes largely independent of the acidic patch, others are dependent on it.
source: Recently, it was shown that while some CHD family remodelers slide nucleosomes largely independent of the acidic patch, others are dependent on it (Dann et al., 2017; Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dann et al., 2017 and Levendosky et al., 2016.

claim: SWI/SNF family enzymes also require the acidic patch for maximal activity.
source: It has been further shown that SWI/SNF family enzymes also require the acidic patch for maximal activity (Dann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dann et al., 2017.

claim: INO80 slides nucleosomes preferentially in the direction of longer flanking DNA and can also create evenly spaced nucleosome arrays.
source: INO80, like ACF, slides nucleosomes preferentially in the direction of longer flanking DNA and can also create evenly spaced nucleosome arrays (Udugama et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Udugama et al., 2011.

claim: The sliding activity of INO80 is thought to be important for positioning the +1 nucleosome at transcription start sites.
source: This sliding activity is thought to be important for positioning the +1 nucleosome at transcription start sites (Krietenstein et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Krietenstein et al., 2016.
